subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Henry Ford's Vision
description: A micro-lesson that makes Henry Ford's Vision usable.

hook.text: In 1900, cars were luxury toys for the rich. Henry Ford wanted to change that completely.

buildup.text: Ford grew up on a farm and hated the backbreaking work. He believed machines could free people.

discovery.text: His mission was simple: build a car so cheap that every worker in his factory could own one.

twist.text: Other carmakers mocked him. Luxury cars had fat margins—why build cheap ones?

climax.text: Ford proved them wrong. By 1927, he had sold 15 million Model Ts—more than all rivals combined.

punchline.text: Ford didn't just make cars. He made them for everyone.

quiz.question: How many Model Ts did Ford sell by 1927?
